description: email.rs handle_email_get (line ~387): DEFAULT_BODY_PROPERTIES.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect() allocates a Vec<String> of 10 items from &'static strs on every call with no bodyProperties argument. The same pattern recurs at line ~1896 for DEFAULT_EMAIL_GET_PROPERTIES. Idiomatic Rust would keep body_properties as Vec<&str> (or &[&str]) throughout the function, only converting to String at the boundary where a String is actually needed. If the downstream code always needs owned Strings, using .map(|&s| s.to_owned()) is clearer than .to_string() on a &&str.
title: body_properties default list uses .map(|s| s.to_string()).collect()
